column3: Names the same two groups and supplies the enduring consequence of their denial.
Specifies the upright written contents carried within the clear proof.
Defines association as a grave false sharing of what belongs to God.
Shows that division followed the arrival of the clear proof.
Identifies the clear proof as a messenger reciting purified sheets.
Parallels a clear Quran and book, supporting proof as disclosed written speech.
Frames denial as continuing uncertainty until an appointed arrival.
Supplies the positive counterpart to the condemned response named in 98:1.
States that the revealed book clarifies the matter over which people differ.
Names the two groups as resisting good sent down from their Lord.
Extends the positive outcome, but adds little to the proof-and-response threshold.
Expresses exclusive devotion without assigning any partner to the Lord.
Connects persistent denial and wrongdoing with loss of guidance.
States the undivided worship and upright religion opposed to divided allegiance.
Boundary evidence: it replaces the given proof with a demanded shortcut.
Applies the Book-people and denial category to a concrete reversal of security.
Boundary evidence of the later summons and the deniers' hardship.
Places association among accountable divided loyalties with distinct outcomes.
Contrast route only; it adds no usable clarification of the focus.
Shows denial as a repeated, intensifying course rather than a single response.
Boundary evidence: no community is indispensable before God.
Shows Book-people acting against believers after truth has become clear.
Provides a one-God and shared-revelation frame for engaging the Book-people.
Adds the adverse end associated with association and hostile expectation.
Offers a general warning about fabricating claims, only indirectly related to denial.
Directly joins messengers' clear proofs, denial, and consequent seizure.
States the unshared devotion that answers the association named in 98:1.
Shows rejection of messengers despite their clear proofs.
Contributes a secondary image of vindication after a person has been denied.
Uses clarification to distinguish truthful and false persons, outside the focus setting.
Limits Book-people status: it gives no control over God's favor.
Rejects partnerhood and every supporting share in divine rule.
Denies that present disbelievers have immunity from earlier communities' outcome.
Shows a pattern of turning away whenever signs arrive.
Uses a written record as judgmental disclosure, secondary to the focus's book.
Makes arrival a final threshold beyond which belief no longer benefits.
Provides a secondary release motif that can illuminate being held until release.
The ritual condition does not clarify the focus's proof or its addressees.
Questions unauthorized claims to write or control the unseen.
The occurrence of ahl here is social and adds no relevant evidence.
Contrasts inherited affiliation with an inwardly inscribed faith commitment.
Legal clarification here does not bear on the focus.
Offers a living knowledge community as a route for inquiry and verification.
Gives a remote limit of disclosure for a Book-people reading.
Presents the sent book as an address that prevents hearers from remaining spectators.
Shows alleged partners failing to provide the connection claimed for them.
Adds a general return of evil schemes, not the focus's proof event.
Shows recipients of a portion of the book choosing error and misguidance.
Separates the messenger's clear delivery from the recipient's response.
Provides only a general condition of change within a people.
Touches family affiliation and hostile expectation, without clarifying the proof.
Places the Book-people deniers within a revealing failed alliance.
Challenges unsupported authority to turn unseen claims into written judgment.
Names Book-people who deny God's signs while witnessing them.
Shows intense approach that still does not become acceptance.
Makes Book-people standing conditional on upholding their scriptures and what is sent.
Supplies a visible horizon encounter as secondary evidence for disclosure.
Its legal setting does not materially clarify the focus's stated threshold.
Directly addresses the deniers as the audience later distinguished by worship.
Shows a Book-people strategy of staged belief and denial toward revelation.
States that devotion to the Lord is not divided among partners.
Portrays denial as an ongoing condition of persistent repudiation.
Questions whether any authority actually speaks for the alleged partners.
Links Book-people and believers to a sign, but only indirectly to 98:1.
Offers a secondary image of an all-encompassing clear record.
Uses the Book-people label in a historical scene without the focus's proof relation.
The shared destination of the fire's people does not clarify the focus.
Presents denial as active, continuing falsification.
Affirms the book's descent from God, supporting its authoritative source.
Shows book recipients embracing false powers and favoring deniers.
Shows deniers reacting with astonishment to the arrival of a warner.
Uses Quranic power and an awaited promise, but not the focus's social distinction.
Provides a secondary account of receptivity, reverence, and forgiveness.
The combat comparison adds no interpretive value for the focus.
Makes clarification a distinct divine act, directly sharpening al-bayyinah.
Broadens 98:4: Book-people differed after knowledge came to them.
Adds only a general recompense for the deniers already covered earlier.
Sets the larger pattern: book and prophets judge disputes, yet division follows clear proofs.
Mentions teaching scripture and wisdom without the focus's response threshold.
Shows a messenger bringing disclosure to Book-people and exposing what was concealed.
Protects good works from being denied, only loosely related to kufr.
Shows demand for further spectacle despite clear proofs already received.
Joins Quranic warning, decisive testimony, and disavowal of association.
Adds a prior pattern of clear signs followed by denial.
Contrast evidence only; it does not clarify the focus's denial or proof.
Gives a concrete association claim and classifies it as denial.
Shows that professed belief can remain internally divided by association.
Its conflict setting does not clarify the proof threshold.
The clear disputant motif is too general to add much after prior evidence.
Reinforces the notion of a clear book, now largely redundant.
Adds a protected book image, secondary to its arrival and reception.
Contrasts argument without knowledge or an illuminating book.
The sovereignty statement lacks a specific route to the focus.
Uses divine clarification in an unrelated legal instruction.
Shows an applied instance of clarified signs and boundaries.
Supplies a dependable written record, remote from the Book-people proof event.
Its devotional instructions do not clarify the focus.
Adds a positive book-record image, not the focus's disclosed proof.
The loyalty test does not add to the stated proof and denial relation.
Completes the denial arc with compelled acknowledgment of truth at punishment.
Shows a confirming book arriving to prior recipients and being met with denial.
Shows refusal to accept a revelation beyond an inherited scriptural boundary.
Depicts book recipients recognizing the messenger yet concealing that recognition.
Condemns concealing clear proofs and guidance after they were made clear in the book.
Connects hiding revealed book content with a destructive exchange.
Addresses Book-people who mix truth with falsehood and conceal truth knowingly.
Describes distortion presented as if it belonged to the book.
Directly addresses Book-people for denying God's signs.
Shows Book-people obstructing believers after knowledge has been received.
Frames Book-people disclosure as a covenant not to conceal the book.
Calls book recipients to believe in the confirming revelation before a decisive reversal.
Addresses Book-people with the messenger's truth and limits claims that divide divine allegiance.
Names a messenger's arrival to Book-people after an interval as removing their excuse.
Presents the Torah as guidance and light while warning against rejecting God's revelation.
Places the confirming book as criterion over earlier scripture and a test of response.
Classifies a concrete association claim as denial and states its consequence.
Warns Book-people against excess and following prior misleading desires.
Shows recipients of the book recognizing the message while the losers deny it.
Contrasts secure belief with belief mixed with association.
Connects scriptural recognition of the messenger with following his disclosed guidance.
Gives Book-people claims that combine denial with divided divine attribution.
Shows religious authorities being treated as rival lords despite the command of one worship.
Presents the Quran as confirming what preceded it and detailing the book.
Combines a clear proof from the Lord with a witnessing recitation and prior book.
Shows differing Book-recipient responses to what has been revealed.
Depicts prior book recipients recognizing and responding to the recited revelation.
States truth from the Lord and preserves the divergent responses of belief and denial.
Records a demand for a sign despite prior evidence in the earlier scriptures.
Challenges association by demanding proof for the rival claims.
Retains the distinct Book-people and associator categories under divine judgment.
Shows those given knowledge recognizing the revelation as truth from their Lord.
States that some book recipients believe the revelation while deniers reject its signs.
Describes it as clear signs held in the knowledge of those given knowledge.
Shows those given knowledge seeing the revelation as truth and guidance.
Joins messengers, clear proofs, scriptures, and illuminating book in one disclosure pattern.
States the book's descent with truth and distinguishes guidance from going astray.
Recalls a messenger bringing clear proofs and a later move into doubt and denial.
Explicitly joins denial of the book with denial of the messengers.
Shows a received book becoming the site of disagreement after its reception.
States that division arose only after knowledge came, through mutual transgression.
Affirms God's sending of the book with truth as the measure of judgment.
Shows a messenger bringing clear proofs while confronting subsequent disagreement.
Uses the Book-people's long delay and hardened hearts as a caution about reception.
Joins messengers, clear proofs, book, and balance in the purpose of revelation.
Places the later messenger within an earlier messenger's announced good news.
States the sending of the messenger with guidance and the religion of truth despite associators' aversion.
Contrasts bearing the Torah with failing to carry out its disclosed responsibility.
